absent: Numeric values of control register, cache, preserve, UART status, BIOS and page mask constants
Register and stack preconditions on entry to relocate and swap routines and ownership of saved control state
UART base address, divisor setup and memory mapped versus port selection policy
Firmware memory map construction, PCI gating variable, and resource tree insertion rules
Platform wallclock operations, MC146818 access timing, and NMI locking internals
Memblock allocation guarantees, mapping checks, early memory copy failure modes, and initrd variable initialization
Boot parameter layout, command line assembly, IMA buffer setup, and sysctl handler semantics

findings.text: Identity mapped kexec transition entry normalizes control registers, reloads page tables, optionally flushes caches, processes a page list, then either wipes most state and returns or calls a peer entry on a dedicated stack and later restores virtual mapping state.

Control register setup first drops CET so write protect can be changed, then requests paging and protected mode while disabling alignment check, write protect, task switch and emulation, then rebuilds CR4 from a saved value keeping only PAE and five level paging plus conditional machine check on TDX guests.

After page processing and a TLB reload used as serialization, behavior forks on a preserve flag: without it all general registers except stack are cleared before return; with it control transfers to a popped entry point, and on return mappings are restored, preserve handling is forced, pages are processed again, then saved stack and control registers and caller state are restored with the peer reentry value returned.

Page list walker consumes eight byte records: one tag selects current destination, another tag follows an indirection page, another tag terminates, and a source tag triggers a page copy; unrecognized records are skipped and iteration continues until termination.

Each source operation copies one full page as quadword units; when preserve context is requested the source, destination and a dedicated swap page are rotated through three copies, otherwise a single direct copy from source to destination occurs.

Two low level character sinks poll a UART status indication for transmitter readiness with a pause in the wait loop, one using port IO around a line status offset and one using memory mapped accesses with scaled register spacing.

Small debug formatters convert a nibble to printable hexadecimal and emit a full quadword as sixteen nibbles followed by newline, delegating each output character through an indirect callable held in a register.

Debug exception table provides sixteen fixed stride entries covering early CPU faults; entries that architecturally lack an error code push a zero placeholder so every path reaches a common handler with exception number and error value on the stack.

Common debug handler spills a subset of registers, initializes debug output, reports fault identity and saved instruction and stack pointers plus spilled and unmodified registers and CR2, returns only for breakpoint via stack cleanup and interrupt return, and otherwise halts in a tight loop.

Debug handler stack layout places saved output and scratch registers at low offsets, then handler pushed exception identity and error, then architectural return frame fields for instruction pointer, code, flags, stack and segment.

Resource clipping leaves non overlapping resources unchanged; on overlap it measures how much lies below and above the excluded interval and retains only the larger remaining side by moving the start or end past the exclusion.
Architecture reservation hook applies only to memory typed availability: it first excludes the high BIOS ROM interval and then excludes firmware memory map intervals through a helper.

Firmware map exclusion iterates all reported entries, clips availability against each address interval, emits informational messages only when clipping changed the range, and is entirely skipped when PCI use of that map is disabled.

Return hook architecture layer exposes a trampoline callback that normalizes trap state and invokes generic handling, a fixup that installs the true return address, and a prepare operation that captures return state and redirects the stack slot to the trampoline.

Trampoline handling forces kernel code segment and trampoline instruction pointer, marks origin as invalid, adjusts stack past pushed state, derives a frame pointer just past trap registers, and copies flags into the segment save slot so a later pop flags plus return sequence works; prepare saves the original stack top and frame before overwriting the top with the trampoline address.

CMOS access uses a volatile lock word plus a spinlock protected RTC lock conceptually; every byte read or write brackets port selection and data transfer with address dependent prefix and suffix operations that serialize against NMI and concurrent access.

Machine CMOS time set and get plus persistent clock update and read form the wall clock layer: set and get translate between epoch based structures and RTC fields, while persistent operations delegate to platform wallclock hooks.

Time set validates the broken down value before writing and reports invalid input or device failure; time get returns zeroed time when firmware trace invalidated the RTC or when the hardware read fails, otherwise normalizes sub second field to zero.

Fallback CMOS RTC platform device has two resources, an IO port interval spanning selection and data ports and a single IRQ, is named for the CMOS RTC driver, and is registered only when no platform RTC device is already present and legacy RTC support is enabled.

Early boot globals track mapped page limits, a bump region bounded by start and end cursors, firmware boot parameters, and four kernel image resources for read only data, data, code and zero initialized storage all marked busy system RAM with initially zero bounds.

CPU and platform info globals include per boot scratch and boot CPU descriptors, firmware tables for power management, interrupt stacks, disk geometry, video and framebuffer state, plus CR4 feature storage and static IMA kexec buffer address and size.

x86 sysctl table exposes NMI panic controls, IO NMI panic control, read only bootloader type and version, IO delay selection, and optionally ACPI video flags, with integer or long handlers and read write or read only modes, registered under the kernel namespace during early init.
Early bump allocator provides aligned extension, reservation of consumed space, and a no operation high mapping cleanup hook.

Bump allocation requires a live region and power of two alignment, rounds the cursor up, checks against a fixed limit, zeroes the granted block, and reservation later marks only the consumed interval and then disables further allocation by clearing the start cursor.

Initrd address and size each combine a low header field with a high extension field and fall back to early physical variables when zero; early reservation keeps the firmware supplied range, while late reservation uses it directly when fully mapped and otherwise allocates a low mapped replacement, copies payload, updates kernel pointers, and frees the original range.
Disk parameter copying has two builds: one duplicates firmware MBR signatures and geometry buffers plus their counts from boot parameters into kernel storage, the other does nothing.

Relocation path depends on cache coherency handling, TLB flushing and serialization around page updates, correct preserve flag handling, dedicated swap and control page stacks, and debug faults other than breakpoint intentionally halt rather than resume.
Page list encoding uses individual low bits to distinguish destination, indirection, completion and source records, aligns addresses to page boundaries, and transfers a page as 512 eight byte units.
Ramdisk option encoding reserves low bits for start selection and dedicates separate high bits for prompt and load requests.
Debug vector area covers sixteen architectural exceptions with uniform handler stride; NMI and fault entries without architectural error codes receive a synthesized zero error value.
Kernel image resources use busy plus system RAM flags; reservation trimming applies to memory typed resources and the BIOS ROM exclusion covers the top of the low address region.
